matchstick.title: Move vertical I-stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Detach a vertical stick that forms an I from one numeral and attach it to another numeral that can accept a vertical stick, ensuring both the source and target remain valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When adjusting the values of numerals could balance the equation, e.g., increasing a numeral by adding an I or decreasing another by removing an I.
matchstick.example: Detaching a vertical stick from an I and attaching it to a V, leaving the V with a single diagonal (invalid).

matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First explore moving a stick within the same character (e.g., V↔X, X↔V, I↔L) before considering moves that affect other characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before trying inter‑character moves.
matchstick.example: Skipping a possible V→X transformation and directly moving a stick to another numeral, missing a valid solution.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After detaching a stick, ensure that both the originating symbol and the destination symbol remain valid Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before evaluating arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and leaving a lone diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A lone diagonal stick does not constitute a valid Roman numeral; V and X require two diagonals, so never leave a single diagonal after a move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a diagonal stick from a V or X.
matchstick.example: Taking one diagonal from a V and not replacing it, resulting in a single diagonal stick.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign, and the removed stick can be reused elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and a minus sign would help balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from a plus sign but discarding the stick instead of reusing it, violating the rule of moving exactly one stick.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character, forming a new numeral (e.g., adding a vertical stick to create I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation lacks a needed numeral and a spare stick can be used to form one.
matchstick.example: Placing a detached stick as a stray line that does not form any valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equality, explore moving a stick from one character to another, ensuring both remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character possibilities without success.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from one numeral to another but leaving the source numeral invalid (e.g., turning X into a single diagonal).

matchstick.title: Swap operators via horizontal stick move
matchstick.principle: The equals sign (=) consists of two horizontal sticks; moving one of them to a minus sign (-) turns the equals into a minus and the minus into an equals, effectively swapping the operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '=' and '-' and a simple operator swap could balance the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' but forgetting to adjust the original '=' to a valid minus, leaving an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: When converting a plus sign to a minus sign by removing its vertical stick, the removed stick can be attached to a numeral that can accept a vertical stick, increasing its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and a numeral could be increased by adding an I.
matchstick.example: Attaching the vertical stick from a plus sign to a numeral that cannot accept a vertical, creating an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick and forming new Roman numerals and operators, compute the numeric values of each side and confirm the equality holds; discard any transformation that does not satisfy the arithmetic.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after a candidate transformation passes symbol validation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Assuming that swapping '=' and '-' yields a correct equation without recomputing the values, resulting in a false equality.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to jump to inter‑character moves, missing simpler intra‑character fixes.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First exhaust all possible intra‑character stick relocations before considering moves between characters.

matchstick.description: Assuming sticks retain their orientation and not rotating horizontals to verticals (or vice versa) when repositioning
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as immutable in orientation, missing valid rotations.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Allow sticks to be reoriented when moved; treat them as generic line segments.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on symbol validity and forgets to check the numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides after a transformation and verify the equation.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., = ↔ -) automatically solve the puzzle
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes structural changes guarantee arithmetic correctness.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After swapping operators, recompute the arithmetic to ensure the equality holds.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the I↔L transformation (adding/removing a horizontal stick to/from an I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overlooks that an I can become an L by adding a horizontal stick, and vice versa.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Consider adding or removing a horizontal stick to/from an I to form L when appropriate.
